title: Diffusion-Inspired Iterative Refinement for Non-Autoregressive Transformer Decoding
one_liner: Treat sequence generation as iterative denoising over discrete tokens so decoding steps are parallel rather than sequential.
description: Proposes a decoding paradigm for Transformers that treats sequence generation as an iterative denoising process over discrete tokens. A corruption schedule progressively masks tokens and the Transformer predicts the clean tokens from the corrupted input in parallel at each step, breaking the sequential bottleneck of auto-regressive decoding. The corruption rate per position and per step is learned rather than fixed, which is the part that distinguishes it from earlier non-autoregressive work.

sections.technique: Discrete corruption process over x_{1:T}: at diffusion step t, mask a subset of tokens according to a learned schedule a_theta(t). The reverse step p_theta(x | x_t, t) is a Transformer predicting logits for every masked position in parallel, with parameters shared across denoising steps.
sections.baselines:
- MaskGit (fixed schedule, single-pass refinement)
- CMLM
- Standard auto-regressive Transformer decoding (quality ceiling)
open_questions: Does a learned per-position corruption schedule actually beat a fixed one, or does the ELBO wash the difference out?
How many denoising steps are needed before the speedup over auto-regressive decoding disappears?
Should the schedule network be trained jointly with the Transformer or in a second stage?
sections.open_risks: The variational bound may be loose enough that the learned schedule collapses to a near-uniform one.
